answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price admission by demand. The fee for each new key is 2 credits times the number of keys admitted in the last ten epochs, so the entry tide sets the price. A farm adding 100 keys in one burst pays 2+4+...+200, about 10,100 credits, while one honest newcomer in a quiet epoch pays a few credits once. The fee sits in an onyx escrow, refunded after 20 epochs of passing answers and forfeited by keys that fail an audit. A falling fee is a public signal that intake is calm. Weakness: a patient farm can trickle keys in, but then it gains only a few per window.
